hero.title: Somebody else's dad knows a solicitor
hero.body: That's a lot of how it works. Not all of it, but more than anyone admits. Below is a list of people who've agreed to answer questions about their job. What it pays. How they got in. What they'd do differently. Nobody's recruiting and there's nothing at the end of it.

items.title: They said yes
items.body: Every name belongs to somebody who agreed to be asked. No stock photos, no careers leaflets.

items.title: Nobody's selling anything
items.body: Ask what it pays. Ask if they hate it. Ask what they'd do differently. There's no pitch at the end of it.

items.title: You can't want a job you've never seen
items.body: Most people end up doing work they happened to watch up close. That's most of the trick, and it isn't about ability.

teasers.title: Three kinds of useful
teasers.body: The list is short so far. These are the people we're asking. If one of them sounds like you, the form is behind that link.
teasers.note: Real names go here as they join.

items.name: Someone three years in
items.quote: You still remember school. That's most of the qualification.

items.name: Someone who runs the place
items.quote: Twenty years of knowing how it actually works. There's no other way to get that.

items.name: Someone who never went to college
items.quote: Paid from the first year. Nobody says that out loud in fifth year.

industries.title: Including the jobs nobody brings up
industries.body: Technology, healthcare, law, finance, trades, media, education, engineering, public sector. Full profiles once your school signs up. The trades are the part worth your time — nobody will tell you they pay you from year one.

cta.title: Your school signs up first
cta.body: Nothing personal. It's how we know you're a student and not somebody else. Tell your guidance counsellor. Five minutes, costs nothing, and they'll be glad of something that isn't a leaflet.
